index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a vertical flowchart illustrating the architectural pipeline of the BERT model, showing the transformation of input tokens into output prediction vectors through three main sequential layers. The global layout is structured as a top-down flow, with components arranged in three horizontal rectangular blocks stacked vertically: 'Input Embeddings' at the bottom, 'Transformer Encoder' in the middle, and 'Prediction Feedforward' at the top. Each block processes six token positions, indicated by aligned inputs and outputs beneath and above each layer respectively.

At the bottom, the 'Input Embeddings' layer receives a sequence of six tokens: '[CLS]', 'this', 'is', '[MASK]', '.', and '[SEP]'. These tokens are mapped to corresponding embedding vectors labeled x₀ through x₅, which are fed upward into the next layer. The 'Transformer Encoder' layer processes these embeddings and produces six intermediate representations labeled y₀ through y₅. These representations are then passed to the topmost layer, 'Prediction Feedforward', which generates final prediction vectors p₀ through p₅, one for each position in the sequence.

Each module is represented as a white rectangular box with black borders and centered black text. The tokens at the bottom are written in plain text, while the embedding vectors (xᵢ), intermediate representations (yᵢ), and prediction vectors (pᵢ) are denoted using bold lowercase letters with subscript indices. All connections between layers are depicted as thin black vertical arrows pointing upward, indicating the forward pass direction of data flow from input to output. There are no horizontal connections or feedback loops; the architecture is strictly feedforward.

The figure caption explicitly states that this is a flow chart of the BERT model illustrating how embedding vectors are transformed into output vectors, reinforcing the purpose of the diagram as a visual explanation of the model’s core processing pipeline. The diagram does not include any color coding or additional annotations beyond the labeled vectors and module names.
